analysis.purpose: knowledge-crib turns a repository into a queryable, provenance-tagged knowledge graph that an AI agent reads INSTEAD of re-reading source. A deterministic pipeline parses code into a committed graph (the soul); a derived index makes it searchable; an agent-authored semantic layer adds MEANING on top, and a trusted memory ledger records what has been learned across sessions. The server itself never calls a model — it queues grounded work, validates what an agent writes back, and serves the result deterministically.
responsibilities: Parse many languages into one shared graph vocabulary, intra-file only, with cross-file resolution as a separate deterministic phase
Store that graph as the single committed source of truth, byte-stable so an unchanged repo re-indexes identically
Derive a rebuildable search index and adjacency model from it, never the reverse
Queue grounded enrichment work for an agent, and reject any claim whose evidence does not appear in the code it cites
Serve bounded, provenance-tagged answers over MCP so an agent can stop reading files
Keep a trusted memory ledger with an explicit gate between observation and team trust

businessRules.rule: The soul is the only source of truth; the search index and dossiers are derived and always rebuildable from it.
businessRules.rationale: A derived artifact that can drift is worse than one that is simply missing.

businessRules.rule: Indexing is deterministic: the same source re-indexes byte-identically, because records are id-sorted within each chunk.
businessRules.rationale: Determinism is what makes the graph diffable, cacheable and safe to commit.

businessRules.rule: Extractors emit only intra-file facts; anything cross-file is resolved in a later phase against the whole graph.
businessRules.rationale: An extractor cannot see other files, so resolving there would mean guessing, and a guess is indistinguishable from a fact downstream.

businessRules.rule: A reference that does not resolve is dropped and counted, never guessed or filled with a placeholder.
businessRules.rationale: A missing edge is honest; a fabricated one silently corrupts every downstream answer.

businessRules.rule: The MCP server never calls a model. It hands an agent grounded work and validates what comes back.
businessRules.rationale: Keeps query latency, cost and reproducibility deterministic, and keeps authored meaning auditable.

businessRules.rule: An authored claim is only verified when an evidence quote actually appears in the span it cites; otherwise it is rejected as hallucination.
businessRules.rationale: This grounding gate is what separates a knowledge graph from a plausible-sounding summary.

businessRules.rule: A node with no authored analysis inherits meaning from its enclosing symbol, then its file, then its cluster — always tagged with where the meaning came from.
businessRules.rationale: Coverage would otherwise require authoring every node; the tag prevents a file purpose being read as a symbol purpose.

businessRules.rule: Responses are token-bounded and report truncation, and every hit reports whether it is grounded in authored meaning or raw code.
businessRules.rationale: A silently trimmed or silently ungrounded answer reads as complete when it is not.

businessRules.rule: Memory is separate from the graph: local observations never become team memory without passing a committed policy gate.
businessRules.rationale: Trust must be granted deliberately and reviewably, not accumulated by writing something down.

businessRules.rule: Secret VALUES never enter the graph — config property keys are surfaced, their values are redacted, and secure files are not read at all.
businessRules.rationale: The graph is committed and searchable, so anything indexed is effectively published.

inputs: Mule and other integration project configs
outputs: A derived search and adjacency index
sideEffects: Writes the graph and derived index under .crib
Installs managed blocks into git hooks and IDE config when asked
errorBehavior: A parser degrades to a file node rather than aborting the run
An unresolvable reference is dropped and counted
A non-git repository falls back from incremental update to a full index
The server keeps serving a slightly stale index rather than dropping the connection
invariants: Same content produces the same id
Every edge endpoint resolves to a real node
Only the soul is authoritative; everything else is derived
Authored meaning is always distinguishable from extracted fact
preconditions: Node 22.5 or later for the built-in SQLite backend
postconditions: After indexing, the graph reflects the source at the recorded commit
risks: Enrichment coverage is authored, so an un-enriched area answers from raw code and reports a low grounded ratio
Language coverage differs per extractor; declared capabilities state what each one does not do
whatToDistrust: Any hit whose grounding is "code" rather than "semantic" — nothing has been authored about it
An inherited purpose describes the owning file or cluster, not the specific node
A stale artifact means the code moved after the analysis was written
